answer: Charge an exponentially rising admission fee for every extra identity that claims rewards in the same epoch: the first slot costs almost nothing, the second doubles, the third quadruples, and so on, with fees burned rather than redistributed. A lone agent at its nadir of activity pays pennies, while a sybil farm trying to flood the lagoon of submissions must pay the geometric sum, which soon exceeds any payout. A knoll of free, low-rate participation remains for newcomers, but bulk claiming becomes self-defeating because each clone adds more cost than the reward it can earn.
